_Original comment by_ **Claudiu Popa (BitBucket: [PCManticore](http://bitbucket.org/PCManticore), GitHub: @PCManticore)**:

---

There are two problems: the first one is that you are reassigning Factory to Factory(...), this being a duplicate for issue #181, which happened before Pylint 1.4. The second one is indeed a new false positive, where we emit not-callable for name.

_Original comment by_ **Gilles Dartiguelongue (BitBucket: [EvaSDK](http://bitbucket.org/EvaSDK), GitHub: @EvaSDK?)**:

---

So the code isn't pretty smart but it works fine and no error was reported with previous release of pylint/astroid.

It seems like pylint is getting confused by the import name overwriting via module scope execution.

```
$ pylint --reports=n test4.py
************* Module test4
L  1: [C0111(missing-docstring), ] Missing module docstring
L  5: [E1120(no-value-for-parameter), ] No value for argument 'self' in unbound method call
```

When aliasing the import in `mod2` or renaming the instantiated object, pylint returns another error:

```
$ pylint --reports=n test4.py
************* Module test4
L  1: [C0111(missing-docstring), ] Missing module docstring
L  5: [E1102(not-callable), ] Factory.name is not callable
```

None of these appeared with pylint-1.3/astroid-1.2. However after applying the same renaming fix, pylint-1.3 showed error E1102 as well.

I have two questions here:
1. can pylint stop being confused about our code doing stupid things like overwriting an imported class name ? If no, this is no biggy, we shall do the renames in our projects.
2. is there a way to make pylint understand that the property is actually returning a callable and there is nothing to fix here ? We discussed the issue internally and we agreed to disagree to un-@property-fy this. I am searching for a better solution but couldn't come up with any yet.

FYI, this kind of code is used to manage SQLAlchemy connections and the property is actually used to store (cache) the result of `sa.orm.sessionmaker` which we need to instantiate only once per backend hence the object creation in module scope.

_Original comment by_ **Claudiu Popa (BitBucket: [PCManticore](http://bitbucket.org/PCManticore), GitHub: @PCManticore)**:

---
1. yes, this is why issue #180 exists. Unfortunately, fixing it is not simple and it will take sometime until I'll find time to investigate (again) what is causing the problem.
2. it's fixable on Pylint's side, probably for Pylint 1.4.1.

_Original comment by_ **Gilles Dartiguelongue (BitBucket: [EvaSDK](http://bitbucket.org/EvaSDK), GitHub: @EvaSDK?)**:

---
1. No problem, I didn't like that overwriting anyway.
2. Will be watching.

_Original comment by_ **Claudiu Popa (BitBucket: [PCManticore](http://bitbucket.org/PCManticore), GitHub: @PCManticore)**:

Check the return of properties when checking for not-callable.

Closes issue #406.

_Original comment by_ **Claudiu Popa (BitBucket: [PCManticore](http://bitbucket.org/PCManticore), GitHub: @PCManticore)**:

---

The second problem was fixed. The first one will be tackled in #181. Thank you for the report.

_Original comment by_ **Gilles Dartiguelongue (BitBucket: [EvaSDK](http://bitbucket.org/EvaSDK), GitHub: @EvaSDK?)**:

---

So I was perplex as to why this patch didn't fix my issue.
Adding some prints all over the place lead me to suspect our property being somewhat different than the testcase I provided and indeed, it is some kind of memoized_property.

Using the attached `mod1v2` as `mod1`, pylint will again raise:

```
L  5: [E1102(not-callable), ] Factory.name is not callable
```

However, using some external module to do the job, like `memoized_property` [1] does not trigger this problem. I guess this is because it is taking another path in astroid's inference.

Is there a sane way to make this work like only considering the last infered node only ?

[1] https://pypi.python.org/pypi/memoized-property/

_Original comment by_ **Claudiu Popa (BitBucket: [PCManticore](http://bitbucket.org/PCManticore), GitHub: @PCManticore)**:

---

Hm, not right now, Pylint will take all your paths for testing. My fix was checking that all of them are returning something that is callable or not.

_Original comment by_ **Gilles Dartiguelongue (BitBucket: [EvaSDK](http://bitbucket.org/EvaSDK), GitHub: @EvaSDK?)**:

---

Ok so the error goes away if I init this attribute in class scope since there is no way for the attribute to return something else than this callable.
Also, as expected, if I add a new return in the property that returns something else than a callable, even if the branch is unreachable, it fails again.
Tricky.

_Original comment by_ **Claudiu Popa (BitBucket: [PCManticore](http://bitbucket.org/PCManticore), GitHub: @PCManticore)**:

---

Yeah, Pylint's inference is kinda dumb in these situations. Choosing branches is a feature that we want, but I don't know when it will land.
